items.message: Linter stdout/stderr appended to a Finding message without sanitisation. A linter that emits ANSI escape sequences, NUL bytes, or very long lines is surface-level cosmetic, but a tool whose output is attacker-influenced (e.g. linting a file containing crafted text) could inject terminal control sequences into whatever display layer renders the finding. The last-20-lines slice limits volume but does not strip control characters.

package.json is read and its `scripts.test` key is used to infer `test_command`, but only the presence of the key is checked — its value is not read. The resulting command is always hardcoded to `("npm", "test")`, so no untrusted content from package.json reaches the command. This is not a finding, but noting it because it differs from what the comments imply about detection fidelity.

The Makefile is read and its target names are extracted with a regex and embedded in `RepoFacts.make_targets`, which `summary()` then joins into a human-readable string displayed by `ls`. A Makefile target name matched by `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+` cannot contain shell metacharacters, so this is not exploitable for injection. However if `make_targets` is ever passed to a shell command (not visible in this diff), the assumption breaks. Flagging as low-confidence because the downstream consumer is not in th…[truncated]

_bind_line inlines `list(facts.test_command)` and `list(facts.lint_command)` directly into the generated scaffold via an f-string using `!r` formatting. Python `repr()` of a list of strings is safe for round-tripping through `compile()`, so there is no code-injection path here. The test at line 282 confirms `compile()` succeeds. Not a finding, but the reliance on `!r` being injection-safe is worth a comment in the code.

Path traversal via the `junit` parameter: `self.junit` is joined to `cwd` with `Path(cwd or ".") / self.junit` and then read. If `junit` is caller-supplied and contains `../../sensitive/path`, `path.read_text()` will follow it. In the current codebase `junit` is set by the adapter constructor from static configuration, not from per-run input, so the immediate risk is low.
